findings.title: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute without related rationale
findings.body: This PR is focused on the annotation cleanup SQL, but this change reduces the top-level cleanup service ticker from every 10 minutes to every 1 minute. That makes all cleanup jobs run ten times as often, which can significantly increase database load and contention, including for the annotation cleanup job this PR is trying to make safer. If this was not intentional, it should be reverted; if it was intentional, it deserves an explicit note in the PR because it is an unrelated behavioral change.

findings.title: Routine annotation cleanup logs full ID batches at error level
findings.body: CleanAnnotations and CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags call r.log.Error after successfully fetching IDs and include the entire ids slice, for example line 534: r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, "cond", cond, "err", err). The err variable is nil at that point because errors return early, so this logs every successful batch as an error. The ids slice can be as large as AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, which the new test sets to 32767, so this can flood error logs with large ID lists and impose significant log I/O/CPU. Log successful progress at debug level without dumping all IDs, and reserve error-level logging for actual errors.

findings.title: SQLite IN-list construction is quadratic
findings.body: deleteByIDs builds the inline SQLite ID list with repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v). Each iteration copies the entire accumulated string, making this O(n²) in the number of IDs. For configured batch sizes like the test's 32767, this can copy gigabytes of string data per batch and make cleanup slow or CPU-spiky on SQLite. A strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt-based construction would avoid the repeated full-string copies.

findings.title: Subtest cleanup is registered after data creation and initial assertions
findings.body: In TestIntegrationAnnotationCleanUp, each subtest calls createTestAnnotations and performs initial count assertions before registering the t.Cleanup function that deletes the rows. If any of those early require calls fail, the cleanup is never installed, leaving data in the shared test database and causing later subtests to fail with confusing cascading assertion errors. The t.Cleanup that deletes annotation and annotation_tag rows should be registered before inserting data for the subtest.
